account: On 8 February 2022, China Daily reported that China Central Television (CCTV) and Baidu AI Cloud had announced an AI sign language anchor and that it was in use during the Beijing 2022 Olympic and Paralympic Winter Games. The report attributes the claims about quality to the company. The XiLing platform converted speech to text and generated the signing shown by the avatar, using a corpus that a Tianjin University of Technology team built with Deaf students. In its account for the International Telecommunication Union (ITU), with information current as of June 2025, Baidu reports that XiLing provided round-the-clock sign-language coverage during the 2022 Winter Olympics, with over 100 million live and replay views. On 9 July 2025, Zheng Xuan, a Deaf professor, wrote in Sixth Tone that his team had back-translated the signing of the Olympic avatars and compared it with the original audio. The team found that key information was lost or distorted and that Deaf viewers had difficulty understanding the signing. He wrote that many Deaf Chinese and sign language interpreters had been skeptical of or resistant to the avatars. His column covers several broadcasters' avatars and does not name Baidu.

ai_role.statement: The AI converted speech to text and generated the signing shown by the avatar, using a corpus that a Tianjin University of Technology team built with Deaf students. A Deaf researcher's team back-translated the Olympic avatars' signing and found that key information was lost or distorted, which places the comprehension problem in the AI-generated signing. The researcher does not name the avatars that his team studied.
